parameters.name: Does something genuinely unique
parameters.evidence: Owns the full preform → fibre → cable chain; hollow-core fibre cutting latency up to 47% for AI links; G.654.E fibre with 30% lower signal loss; 785+ patents

parameters.name: Can't easily copy
parameters.evidence: Preform lines take years and heavy capex to build, and hyperscaler qualification is a multi-year audit — but cable itself is copyable and Chinese supply is long

parameters.name: Quality over quantity
parameters.evidence: Optical-connectivity attach rate targeted above 20% now and 25% by FY27 — more value per metre, not more metres; data centres ~53% of revenue

parameters.name: Discipline on volume
parameters.evidence: The plan is explicitly volume: ₹20,000 Cr by FY29 and +50% capacity. What changed is that the volume is contracted, not tendered

parameters.name: Customer satisfaction / retention
parameters.evidence: A hyperscaler qualified STL as a second source — a multi-year audit — plus repeat Neuralis orders of US$100 Mn+ and a further US$288 Mn high-density cable agreement on 29 Aug 2026. No churn or NPS data is disclosed

parameters.name: R&D investment
parameters.evidence: 785+ patents, five laboratories, hollow-core and G.654.E commercialised, and an EPO appeal that revoked Fujikura's EP3796060 outright. R&D is not a separately disclosed P&L line

parameters.name: Free cash flow
parameters.evidence: Not disclosed as a line item; capex is ₹1,000 Cr/yr against ₹756 Cr TTM PAT; the ₹703 Cr net cash came from a ₹1,500 Cr QIP, not from operations

parameters.name: Debt management
parameters.evidence: Net cash ₹703 Cr, borrowings ₹989 Cr, and the equity was raised before the capex; ICRA AA (stable)

parameters.name: Management stability
parameters.evidence: Ankit Agarwal has been at STL since 2007, CEO since 2021 and MD since 2024; the promoter family chairs the board; Lakshya has been consistent across three calls

parameters.name: Capital allocation
parameters.evidence: Right sequence this cycle (QIP → deleverage → capex), but the last five years delivered −0.3% revenue CAGR and two loss years

moat.binding_constraint: Free cash flow (1.5) and volume discipline (2.0) — a technical moat that has not yet converted into cash
moat.verdict: STL owns a real piece of the optical chain — the preform, the fibre recipe and the patents around them — and that is worth a narrow moat, not a wide one. At 3.3/5 the franchise is better than its five-year record; ₹827 assumes the record has already caught up.

dcf_assumptions.template: AlphaSpread base case (price-independent); DCF is the official intrinsic value

valuation.methodology: AlphaSpread, accessed 25 Oct 2026: DCF ₹110.31, multiples ₹278.66, official intrinsic ₹110.31, buy zone ₹88.24 (IV − 20% MOS). Blended = equal weight of DCF and multiples = ₹194.49; blended buy zone ₹155.59. Forward cross-check: FY29E EPS ₹51.0 × 18× = ₹918. The spread is the bet: trailing cash flow says −87%, the FY29 plan says +11%.

trends.reconciliation: Screener's −43% 3-yr profit box uses its own trailing windows; the clean FY23→FY26 print CAGR (₹127 Cr → ₹56 Cr) is −23.9%. The +18,631% TTM profit box is an off-tiny-base artifact (−₹123 Cr FY25 → +₹756 Cr TTM).

anchor.opm: 21.2% TTM (Q2 FY27 operational EBITDA 27.1%, reported 33.5% incl. ₹161 Cr tariff refund)
anchor.guidance: ₹20,000 Cr revenue by FY29 (4× FY26) · >30% EBITDA margin FY29 · capex ₹1,000 Cr/yr · ₹32,253 Cr of book scheduled Q4 FY27 onward

logic: Base tracks Lakshya, delivered about two years late: revenue ₹23,579 Cr by FY31 at a 16.5% PAT margin, profit grows 5.1× while the multiple compresses 56× → 22× — and the stock still pays 15% a year.

Bear is a disappointment case, not a collapse: the US LTA runs without a second win, telecom tender pricing returns, margin settles near 15%, and the market pays 15× for a cable maker — revenue still compounds at 15%.
Bull: data-centre demand outruns capacity, a second and third hyperscaler qualify STL, preform stays tight, and the market keeps 28× on ₹132 of EPS.

Earnings do more work than the multiple: FY31 EPS spans 4.7× while price spans 8.8×. Base EPS at 15× still gives ₹1,136; Bear EPS at 22× gives ₹614 — conviction about volume, not the exit multiple, decides the stock.

takeaway.core_idea: An integrated optical-fibre maker — one of the few outside China that draws its own preform — that has re-based itself onto AI data-centre demand
takeaway.what_changed: From a telecom tender-taker that lost ₹180 Cr across FY24–25 to a hyperscaler supplier with a ₹35,274 Cr book and a 27% operational margin
takeaway.hidden_signal: The mix did it, not the price: data centres at ~53% of revenue and preform integration are what turned a 10% margin into 27% in five quarters
takeaway.what_breaks: One customer, one award, ₹1,000 Cr/yr of capex and a 56× trailing multiple — four ways for the same story to stall
takeaway.open_question: Can STL convert a ₹35,274 Cr book into 27%+ margins and a second hyperscaler before the multiple normalises?
takeaway.moat: 3.3/5 — narrow, not wide. The edge is technical (preform, hollow-core, 785+ patents); the weaknesses are cash conversion and volume discipline
takeaway.verdict: Own the turn, not the price. The operating story is real; ₹827 already assumes it lands — and prices a narrow moat as if it were wide.
takeaway.one_line: STL spent three years losing money in a tendered telecom market and one year winning hyperscaler contracts — the ₹35,274 Cr book says the demand is real, and ₹827 says you are paying today for FY29 execution.
